summary.text: Pumice is a volcanic rock made of extremely bubbly, rough-textured volcanic glass, and it is usually light in color.
It forms when hot, pressurized rock is blasted out of a volcano: the sudden pressure drop lets dissolved gases form bubbles, and fast cooling freezes them in place.
Because pores take up 64–85% of its volume, pumice floats on water, possibly for years, until it becomes waterlogged and sinks.

facts.label: Name origin
facts.value: Latin pumex, related to spuma, meaning foam

facts.label: Krakatoa rafts
facts.value: Drifted the Indian Ocean for up to 20 years

facts.label: Black pumice
facts.value: Colored by tiny scattered magnetite crystals

items.prompt: You drop a typical chunk of pumice into a bucket of water. What happens?

options.label: It sinks straight to the bottom
It slowly dissolves into the water

items.explain: Most of pumice's volume is pore space, so it floats, possibly for years, until it fills with water and sinks.

items.prompt: Opening a fizzy drink makes bubbles appear. What plays the same role when pumice forms?
items.explain: As the rock is ejected, falling pressure lowers how much gas can stay dissolved, so the gases come out as bubbles, as CO₂ does in an opened drink.

items.prompt: Gas bubbles form in erupting rock. What keeps them trapped inside pumice instead of escaping?

options.label: Minerals that grow and seal each hole
Water that fills and plugs the holes
The weight of ash piled on top
Fast cooling that sets the rock around them

items.explain: Cooling and depressurization happen at the same time, freezing the bubbles in a glassy matrix.

items.prompt: An underwater volcano erupts. What can it create at the sea surface that endangers ships?

options.label: A slick of thick black oil
A sheet of solid sea ice

items.explain: Pumice from an underwater eruption can reach the surface and form rafts that are a hazard for ships.

items.prompt: You find a dark, heavy volcanic rock with big holes and thick walls between them, and it sinks in water. What is it most likely?
items.explain: Scoria differs from pumice by having larger vesicles, thicker walls, a dark color and greater density, and it often sinks.

items.prompt: Two volcanoes erupt bubbly rock. One magma is thick and sticky; the other is runny. Which is more likely to make pumice?
items.explain: Pumice forms when gas bubbles stay trapped in viscous magma as it cools to glass; runnier magma gives scoria instead.
